assets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: production rig-parts atlas for a friendly forest squirrel neighbor in the existing hand-painted 2D children's adventure. The input is a STYLE reference: match its warm illustrated shading, charming proportions and clean watercolor-like painted forms, but create a squirrel, not a human. Character: warm cinnamon squirrel with cream cheeks and belly, soft expressive dark eyes, tiny rounded ears, a sage-green keeper's apron with acorn-key pocket, cream shirt, small brown feet. Friendly woodland camp caretaker, full side-three-quarter view facing RIGHT. Six separate parts on a transparent 3-column by 2-row canvas, each part entirely inside its own cell with at least 40px blank space to every cell edge. TOP LEFT: complete torso from a short neck down to two planted feet, wearing apron/shirt, NO head, NO forearms/hands and NO tail, open rounded hidden shoulder caps. TOP MIDDLE: one complete head facing right with open eyes, visible soft furry neck, no body. TOP RIGHT: the exactly same head with eyes gently closed for blinking, same scale and angle. BOTTOM LEFT: one entire near arm from rounded shoulder through elbow to relaxed mitten paw, cream sleeve, bent slightly, no body. BOTTOM MIDDLE: another identical style near arm with raised paw for a greeting wave, no body. BOTTOM RIGHT: large fluffy S-shaped squirrel tail with rounded attachment base at bottom left. The parts are designed to overlap so hide cut ends with soft fur/sleeve texture: no exposed black sockets, no outlined cut caps, no mechanical joints. Each part must be isolated, no labels, no frames, no shadows cast outside, no checkerboard, no scenery. Painterly game asset quality, not vector, not plastic 3D, no pixel art. Exact 3x2 layout, genuinely transparent background, landscape.
assets.packaging: Generated PNG preserved. Runtime atlas rectangles and anchor transforms only; no alpha extraction or repaint by Python.
